title: Bagel and Lox Breakfast Board
subtitle: Toasted bagels with lox, cream cheese, capers, and fixings for ten.
description: Toasted bagels with lox, cream cheese, capers, and fixings laid out for self-serve. A lighter hall breakfast that still feels like a treat when the budget allows.

steps.title: Prep all fixings
steps.instruction: Slice onion, tomato, and cucumber and arrange in separate bowls on ice or cold trays. Drain capers and portion cream cheese into ramekins. Keep lox refrigerated until the board goes out.

steps.title: Toast the bagels
steps.instruction: Split bagels and toast on sheet pans at 350°F until edges are crisp, about 6 minutes. Hold in a warm oven uncovered at 200°F—do not stack or they steam soft.

steps.title: Arrange the board
steps.instruction: Center lox on a large chilled platter folded in overlapping layers. Surround with ramekins of cream cheese, capers, onion, tomato, cucumber, and lemon wedges.

steps.title: Set the line
steps.instruction: Place toasted bagels in a warm basket at the line with tongs. Post a simple build order: schmear, lox, capers, onion, tomato.

steps.title: Serve and refresh
steps.instruction: Serve immediately as a self-serve board. Refresh lox and cold fixings on ice if service runs longer than 30 minutes to keep fish food-safe.

stationWorkflow: Keep lox on ice until the moment the board hits the table—room temp fish is a food-safety issue.
Toast bagels in two sheet pan batches so all ten finish crisp at the same time.
Assign one crew member to restock fixings while another manages bagel refills.
cleanupNotes: Discard any lox held above 40°F for more than 2 hours—do not save for later shifts.
Wash onion and caper boards separately from bagel crumbs to avoid cross-smells.
leftovers: Unused cream cheese and capers keep; repurpose lox in scrambled eggs within 24 hours if chilled.
Day-old bagels make excellent French toast sticks with cinnamon sugar.

adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free bun/bread and toast on a separate, clean surface.
